asset_explanations.caption: Figure 4: Overview of the proposed 3MFact framework, comprising five components: Video Descriptor (video-to-text conversion), Claim Verifier (assesses evidence sufficiency), Question Manager (generates questions and retrieves answers), Information Retriever (searches for evidence), and Reasoner (synthesizes judgment with rationale and evidence).
asset_explanations.summary: The figure displays the architecture of the 3MFact framework, a multi-stage pipeline for video fact-checking. It features five main components: Video Descriptor, Claim Verifier, Question Manager, Information Retriever, and Reasoner. The process begins with input data (c, B, v) being processed by the Video Descriptor to generate a summary 't', which is then evaluated by the Claim Verifier. Based on the verifier's output (alpha), the system either routes the task directly to the Reasoner or to the Question Manager. The Question Manager interacts with the Information Retriever to fetch evidence and generates answers using either video analysis or retrieved text evidence.

asset_explanations.caption: Table 3: Comparison of Models for 2-Class Classification. Trad.: traditional methods; LLM.: LLM-based approaches. 3MFact $ _{(C+V)} $ uses CogVLM (Wang et al. 2023) as ImageLMM and VideoLLaVa as VideoLMM, and 3MFact $ _{(M+M)} $ uses MiniCPM-V 2.6 as both ImageLMM and VideoLMM.
asset_explanations.summary: This table reports performance metrics (Accuracy, Recall, Precision, F1) for five models on a 2-class classification task. Traditional methods (SV-FEND) and LLM-based approaches (VideoLLaVa, MiniCPM-V 2.6, two variants of 3MFact) are compared. The 3MFact model variant using MiniCPM-V for both image and video (3MFact_(M+M)) achieves the highest F1 score.

supported_claims.claim: 3MFact_(M+M) achieves the highest F1 score (73.85%) among all models.
VideoLLaVa has the highest recall (95.40%) but the lowest accuracy (44.11%).
MiniCPM-V 2.6 has the lowest recall (20.81%) and the second lowest F1 (30.90%).
3MFact_(M+M) achieves the highest precision (71.93%) among all models.
The two 3MFact variants outperform all other models on F1 score, with both exceeding 69%.
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Comparison of F1 values across rows: 3MFact_(C+V)=69.81%, 3MFact_(M+M)=73.85%, next best is VideoLLaVa=57.84%.

possible_misreadings.claim: VideoLLaVa is the worst performing model overall.
possible_misreadings.why_wrong: Although VideoLLaVa has the lowest accuracy (44.11%), it has the highest recall (95.40%) and a moderate F1 (57.84%), outperforming MiniCPM-V 2.6 on F1. Thus, 'worst' depends on the chosen metric.

possible_misreadings.claim: 3MFact_(M+M) is the best model for all classification tasks.
possible_misreadings.why_wrong: The table only evaluates 2-class classification. Performance may differ on multi-class or other datasets/tasks.

possible_misreadings.claim: Traditional methods are inferior to LLM-based methods.
possible_misreadings.why_wrong: SV-FEND (traditional) achieves a higher accuracy (62.80%) than VideoLLaVa (44.11%) and MiniCPM-V 2.6 (62.73%), and its F1 (38.56%) is higher than MiniCPM-V 2.6 (30.90%). So not all LLM methods outperform the traditional one.

limitations: Only 2-class classification results are shown, not multi-class or other tasks.
Only five models are compared; results may not generalize to other models or datasets.
Metrics are reported without confidence intervals or statistical significance tests.
The caption indicates use of specific base models (CogVLM, VideoLLaVa, MiniCPM-V) but does not detail training or evaluation procedures.
